test: 42 install.sh refuses a Condition*= that would turn a failure into a silent skip
why: a condition that does not hold marks the job SUCCESSFUL, so OnFailure= is never reached. Both scheduled units shipped one on the very EnvironmentFile whose absence is supposed to page
old:
say "checking no unit carries a Condition*= that would turn a failure into a silent skip"
for u in ${UNITS}; do
  cond="$(grep -E '^Condition[A-Za-z]+=' "${UNIT_DIR}/${u}" || true)"
  [ -z "${cond}" ] \
    || die "${u} has ${cond}; a condition that does not hold marks the job SUCCESSFUL, so OnFailure= never fires. Remove it."
done

why: grep anchors ^ and $ to a LINE, so $'48\nfoo' passed the digits-only rule, the -gt comparison then errored to false, and the drill printed DRILL PASSED on a 30-day-old snapshot
old:

esac

test: 34b backup.sh creates a missing destination directory 0700
why: REVIEW ITEM 11: with the umask set after the mkdir, a hand-run that CREATES the destination leaves it at the ambient umask, and the file names in a backup directory are an inventory of the vault

test: 45 restore.sh --compose restores onto a fresh host with no container yet
why: REVIEW ITEM 6: `docker compose cp` needs a container to EXIST, and on the total-host-loss case this procedure is written for, none does. Without the create the documented restore fails with 'no container found' in exactly the situation it exists for
old:
if [ -z "$(docker compose ps -aq "${SERVICE}" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    echo "no ${SERVICE} container yet (fresh host); creating it stopped so the volume exists..."
    if ! docker compose create "${SERVICE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "error: could not create the ${SERVICE} container; check docker-compose.yml and .env" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
  fi

test: 45/47 the restored database is owned by the service user
why: REVIEW ITEM 6: docker compose cp writes the file as the host user, the service runs unprivileged, and without --user 0 the chown cannot run at all, so the app starts and crash-loops on its first write right after a disaster recovery

test: 49 restore.sh --compose refuses when the service user cannot write
why: REVIEW ITEM 6: the chown succeeding is not the same as the service user being able to write (a compose file that pins user: to another id is enough). Without this the script reports a successful restore of a database the app cannot open
old:
if ! docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh "${SERVICE}" -c \
      'test -w /app/data/trustissues.db'; then
    echo "error: the restored database is not writable by the service user; the app would crash-loop" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
